newsitem.title: UK: Mark keeps soft tone in Europe amid EMU optimism.
newsitem.headline: Mark keeps soft tone in Europe amid EMU optimism.

text.p: The mark continued to edge lower on its crosses in late European trade, pressured by growing optimism towards monetary union which was underscored by a cut in key Portuguese interest rates today.
Dollar strength also contributed to the mark's woes and though off its earlier highs, the bullish dollar mood helped keep EMU optimism on the boil.

"The dollar tone is positive which should keep the mark on the defensive," said Jeremy Stretch, currency strategist at NatWest Markets in London. "The EMU project will need a strong dollar to get off the ground so this is helping EMU sentiment, but it's a bit pre-emptive to say the convergence trade is fully back on track."

Benign inflation data today from France and Spain kept rate cut expectations for those countries simmering but it was Portugal that led the way today with a 20 basis point cut in its repo rate to 6.30 percent.
The Bank of Portugal also cut its drain rate 40 basis points to 5.8 percent and emergency lending rate 50 basis points to 7.8 percent.
Dealers said the cut was widely expected but it added further to European bond market strength and also served to tighten yield spreads over Germany.
Mark/escudo touched its lowest levels since January, trading at 99.93/96 against 100.13/16 escudos late Thursday.
Mark/peseta was also at its lowest levels since January and stood at 84.22/25 against 84.44/46 pesetas.

Comments today from EU Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy expecting EMU to start on time with many countries heightened monetary union expectations. He said many countries had shown substantial budget discipline, including Italy, Spain and Portugal.
His comments followed earlier remarks from Bank of France council member Paul Marchelli who said Italy, Spain and Portugal should be in from EMU's start.
Marchelli also said he believed Germany wanted an excessively strong euro. A broad-based EMU resulting in a weaker euro would be good for employment in Europe, he said.
"Those comments really back up the market view that EMU is going ahead on time and is likely to be broad," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International in London.
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl expressed his optimism of Germany meeting EMU criteria which, along with timetable, was not open to negotiation, he said.

But Bundesbank board member Edgar Meister raised his doubts that Bonn would meet the deficit criteria. He also stressed that convergence was more important than deadlines which would imply a smaller group of participants at EMU's start.
Mark/lira steadied around the day's lows in late trade, shrugging off the recent political storm in Italy this week over the sending of an Italian-led security force to Albania.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi faces a confidence vote in Italy's lower house Saturday which he is expected to survive as he did in Thursday's vote in the Senate.
"The market doesn't see this political situation as impinging on Italy's fiscal retrenchment," said IBJ's Francis.

The lira did see a week of choppy trade but overall ranges were tight, said dealers, reflecting the relative market calm to this latest political crisis. Italian BTPs were firmer which also saw the Bund/BTP spread narrow even further.
Mark/lira was trading at 985.15/35 from 989.55/85 Thursday.
Mark/Swiss slipped to its lowest levels since December of last year, edging down to 85.08/11 centimes in late trade from 85.53/56 centimes per mark Thursday.
Mark/Swedish crown also rode the rest of the pack lower, slipping to 4.4595/25 crowns from 4.4810/40.
Mark/French franc steady at lower levels and stood at 3.3642/45 against 3.36551/56.
-- Andrew Reierson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 6745
